children: Rep.
Ro Khanna
(D-Calif.) criticized President
Donald Trump’s
Venezuela policy, accusing the administration of reviving an imperialist approach to foreign policy and abandoning America’s commitment to decolonization.
Khanna Calls Trump Policy ‘Gunboat Diplomacy
On Saturday, Khanna posted on
X
while sharing a clip of his interview with MS NOW, where he criticized Trump’s reported actions involving Venezuela and its oil reserves.
"Trump’s foreign policy has rolled back the clock a hundred years to the era of gunboat diplomacy where might makes right," the California Democrat wrote.
He added, "It’s not just that it’s strategically wrong. It’s morally wrong."
In the interview, Khanna said the situation was "sad to see" and argued that the U.S. was returning to a foreign policy model it should have left behind.
"It’s like we’ve rolled back the clock 100 years to the era of gunboat diplomacy," he said, pointing to U.S. actions in Guatemala, El Salvador and Haiti.
"It’s wrong to have a colonial model of the world," he added.
The White House did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for a comment.
Khanna Accuses Trump of Reversing Decolonization
Khanna also referenced his grandfather, who he said was jailed twice while fighting for Indian independence from Britain.
"I thought America had stood for decolonization," he said, citing former President
Franklin D. Roosevelt’s
push for British Prime Minister
Winston Churchill
to decolonize.
"Trump is rolling it all back because he simply believes in a world where might makes right, where you take what you can," Khanna said.
